insights.headline: RBI hikes repo rate to 5.50% with 'calibrated tightening'; bullion soft ahead of Fed minutes
insights.summary: The RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% on October 7 with a 'calibrated tightening' stance, as inflation runs above the 4% target; analysts note the move need not weaken gold, which tracks US rates, the dollar and the rupee more closely. MCX gold opened lower around Rs 1.49 lakh per 10 grams ahead of the Fed's September meeting minutes, with traders pricing an 85% probability of a December US rate hike. Official buying stayed firm: the PBOC added 740,000 ounces in September, its biggest monthly increase in three years and 23rd straight month of purchases.
points: RBI raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% with a 'calibrated tightening' stance; higher rates can support the rupee, which feeds into domestic gold prices.
MCX gold opened lower on Oct 7 ahead of the Fed's September minutes; December futures were near Rs 1.49 lakh/10g.
The GST Council is weighing 3% IGST on bullion imports by banks and nominated agencies, ending MMTC/STC's tax advantage.
China's central bank added 740,000 oz of gold in September — its largest monthly addition since September 2023.
Diwali buying looks cautious: gold is down ~Rs 8,000/10g over a month, with buyers preferring light jewellery.

trending.title: Rate calls dominate bullion's week
trending.summary: The RBI's 25-bps hike and the Fed minutes due Wednesday frame every gold and silver move — domestic prices are caught between tighter local policy and US rate-hike odds.

trending.title: Central banks keep stacking gold
trending.summary: The PBOC's biggest monthly gold addition in three years and 39 net tonnes of August buying confirm official-sector demand is still a pillar of the market.

trending.title: Diwali demand stays selective
trending.summary: Prices are down about Rs 8,000 per 10g in a month, but buyers stay price-shy — lighter jewellery and token purchases rule as Diwali nears.

trending.title: Silver's split signals
trending.summary: Silver hovers near record highs domestically while analysts warn its supply deficit is getting harder to fix as copper ore tightens.

items.title: RBI Repo Rate Hike: Will Gold Prices Fall After Rates Rise To 5.50%? What Investors Should Know
items.summary: The RBI raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% on October 7, shifting its stance to 'calibrated tightening' as inflation runs above the 4% target. Experts quoted in the piece say the hike doesn't automatically weaken gold: US interest rates, real yields, the dollar and the rupee matter more for bullion prices.

items.title: Gold prices dip Rs 1,500/10 grams; silver down Rs 1,600/kg ahead of Fed minutes. Key levels to track
items.summary: MCX bullion opened lower on October 7 as traders awaited the US Fed's September meeting minutes: December gold futures dipped to about Rs 1,49,505 per 10 grams and silver eased to about Rs 2,25,651 per kg. Spot gold held near $4,150 an ounce; the minutes are expected to clarify how much support remains for further US rate hikes, with traders pricing an 85% probability of a December hike.

items.title: MMTC, STC may lose gold import tax advantage as GST Council weighs 3% GST
items.summary: The GST Council is likely to discuss on October 8 bringing government trading entities like MMTC and STC under the 3% GST net for precious-metal imports, ending a tax advantage held since 2017 and putting banks, nominated agencies and bullion exchanges on the same footing, the Times of India reports.

items.title: China posts biggest monthly gold reserve increase in 3 years
items.summary: The People's Bank of China added 740,000 ounces of gold in September, lifting reserves to 77.47 million ounces — the largest monthly increase since September 2023 and the 23rd consecutive month of buying. China's foreign-exchange reserves dipped $38.1 billion to $3.4 trillion over the same month.

items.title: Gold edges lower with focus on Fed minutes, rate path clues
items.summary: Spot gold eased 0.3% to $4,150 an ounce as investors awaited minutes from the Fed's September meeting for clues on further rate hikes. Fed officials Mary Daly and Jeff Schmid both stressed inflation control, and traders still price an 85% chance of a December hike. The minutes could reshape hike odds and move Treasury yields, the dollar and oil, analysts say.

items.title: Gold, silver prices: What is weighing on precious metals and what investors should watch
items.summary: Gold and silver slipped as a stronger US dollar and elevated US Treasury yields weighed on bullion; domestic gold eased about Rs 200 to Rs 1.49 lakh per 10 grams on October 6 while silver stayed near record highs. The piece lays out the key price levels and the upcoming US data and Fed-rate signals Indian investors should track.

items.title: Rupee loses 13 paise to close at 96.42 per US dollar
items.summary: The rupee closed 13 paise lower at 96.42 against the US dollar as foreign fund outflows weighed on the currency. Traders are watching the RBI's policy decision, with markets pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike amid mounting inflation risks.

items.title: Gold price dips, but buyers remain cautious ahead of Diwali
items.summary: Gold has fallen roughly Rs 8,000 per 10 grams over the past month to about Rs 1.47 lakh (excluding GST), yet buyers in Pune remain cautious ahead of Diwali. Shoppers are choosing lighter jewellery and smaller token purchases, while jewellers report steady festive-season footfall.

items.title: Gold to hit $5,000, silver $97 in the next 12 months - LBMA delegate survey
items.summary: Delegates at the 2026 LBMA Global Precious Metals Conference expect gold near $5,013 an ounce a year from now, about 20% above current spot, and silver near $94.70, Kitco reports; a UBS survey found 65% of reserve managers cite diversification as the main reason for holding gold.

items.title: Central banks add 39 net tonnes of gold in August with China, Uzbekistan and Poland leading purchases
items.summary: Central banks kept up strong gold buying in August with 39 net tonnes added, led by China, Uzbekistan and Poland, World Gold Council data show. Senior research lead Marissa Salim noted other banks also repatriated or moved bullion to new vaults. The pace confirms official demand remains firm even with gold near record highs.

items.title: NYSE Owner Starts Gold Futures in London, a Market Without One Since 2022
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange has begun offering gold futures trading in London, the latest attempt to bring derivatives to the centre of the world's physical bullion trade. The NYSE owner debuted precious-metals contracts tied to London's daily auction prices, giving the $190-billion-a-day market its first futures since 2022.

items.title: Silver's Supply Deficit Is Getting Harder to Fix as Copper Ore Tightens
items.summary: An Investing.com analysis argues silver's supply deficit is becoming harder to close as tightening copper ore supply constrains new output, with most silver mined as a by-product of copper and other base metals. The piece says the structural shortfall continues to underpin silver even as prices consolidate.

items.title: Gold-silver ratio at 68: Gold looks expensive, but should investors stay invested?
items.summary: The gold-silver ratio has risen to about 68:1, leaving gold looking expensive relative to silver, Moneycontrol reports; analysts quoted in the piece suggest long-term investors keep gold as the core holding and consider adding silver if the ratio starts declining with improving silver demand.

items.title: Gold corrects 26% from January record high | Is this a buying opportunity ahead of Diwali?
items.summary: Gold has corrected more than 26% from its January peak of $5,595 an ounce to around $4,100, one of its sharpest drawdowns in years, with MCX gold back below ₹1.50 lakh per 10 grams. Kotak Securities' Kaynat Chainwala traces the slide to firm inflation prints pushing Fed hike bets near 90%, while Tata Mutual Fund says central-bank buying and geopolitical uncertainty keep structural drivers intact.

items.title: Gold, Silver Edge Higher On MCX As Fed Rate-Hike Bets Ease
items.summary: Bullion edged higher on MCX after softer US jobs data eased October Fed rate-hike bets; December gold futures traded around ₹1,49,212 per 10 grams and December silver near ₹2,26,322 per kg by mid-afternoon, though elevated Treasury yields capped gains ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting.

items.title: Gold, silver edge higher on MCX: Key levels to watch
items.summary: Gold and silver traded higher on MCX on Tuesday, extending the recovery from September's correction as soft US payrolls eased October Fed-hike bets; analysts flagged key support and resistance levels to watch ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting.
